narrativeReportMd:
# SubstanceSourceMaterial R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`SubstanceSourceMaterial` is a hard breaking removal as a standalone resource: R4 instances with `resourceType: "SubstanceSourceMaterial"` have no same-name R6 StructureDefinition target. The likely R6 replacement is only a partial, embedded component, `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`.

## Scope
I compared the R4 assigned StructureDefinition against the R6 package index and R6 substance-related StructureDefinitions. I excluded inherited base-resource changes and treated `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` only as an inferred migration target.

## Main migration themes
The dominant issue is artifact identity loss. Systems that stored, validated, searched, generated classes for, or exchanged `SubstanceSourceMaterial` resources must move to a different resource model. The candidate R6 component is narrower: it keeps type, genus, species, part, and country of origin, but drops or relocates many R4 details such as source material class/state, organism identifiers and names, parent substance identifiers/names, fraction descriptions, detailed taxonomy, hybrid data, and part location.

## Highest-impact findings
The resource removal is the highest-impact finding. The second major risk is lossy migration into `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`. A separate terminology risk exists because the candidate R6 `countryOfOrigin` has a required country ValueSet binding where R4 declared no local binding.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed to decide the intended R6 target for each R4 data category, especially fraction, parent-substance, detailed taxonomy, and hybrid data. The local package did not include an official cross-version map.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive design could have retained a deprecated `SubstanceSourceMaterial` resource or provided an explicit cross-version extension/profile mapping while encouraging migration to `SubstanceDefinition`. Because the R4 resource was draft/FMM 0, removal may be justified, but the absence of a computable migration map leaves implementers with non-trivial manual work.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `SubstanceDefinition` as its own artifact and review source-material terminology expansions and any official cross-version maps if available.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `SubstanceSourceMaterial` is absent from the R6 ballot package, making existing R4 instances and generated resource types incompatible with R6. The main migration concerns are resource identity removal, lossy collapse into `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`, and a newly required country binding on the likely mapped country element. The largest uncertainty is the lack of an official cross-version mapping.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not a field-by-field version bump. Implementers should plan a remodel from standalone source-material resources into `SubstanceDefinition` records, preserve unmapped details with extensions or other SubstanceDefinition structures where appropriate, and normalize country codes if using the R6 sourceMaterial component.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the assigned R6 resource is absent and that `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` is the closest local successor, because the package index and substance-related StructureDefinitions were inspected. Confidence is medium for exact element-level migration recommendations because no official diff, ConceptMap, StructureMap, or narrative migration guidance was available.

findings.title: SubstanceSourceMaterial was removed as a standalone R6 resource

oldState.summary: R4 defines a concrete, non-abstract `SubstanceSourceMaterial` resource.

semanticText.short: Source material shall capture information on the taxonomic and anatomical origins as well as the fraction of a material.
semanticText.definition: The R4 resource captures taxonomic and anatomical origins and fractions of source materials, particularly for naturally derived polymers, structurally diverse substances, and herbal preparations.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has a resource identity, canonical URL, resourceType, generated class/API surface, and validation target for `SubstanceSourceMaterial`.

newState.summary: No R6 `StructureDefinition/SubstanceSourceMaterial` exists in the local R6 core package.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 package contains `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition`, but no same-name `SubstanceSourceMaterial` StructureDefinition. The closest observed source-material content is an embedded component, `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`.

facts.note: No same-id R6 StructureDefinition was present.
The R6 package index has no entry for this canonical URL.
Inferred from the R6 substance-related StructureDefinitions and matching source-material terminology.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The assigned R6 file is absent and the R6 index only lists `StructureDefinition-Substance.json` and `StructureDefinition-SubstanceDefinition.json` for substance resources. `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` preserves the source-material concept and references source-material ValueSets, making it the strongest local migration candidate, but it is not a resource-level rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and runtime break. An R4 JSON/XML instance whose `resourceType` is `SubstanceSourceMaterial` has no R6 core StructureDefinition to validate against. Generated SDKs, serializers, REST endpoints, search parameters, database tables, and switch statements that expect this resource type will fail unless they are explicitly migrated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The resource is specialized and draft/FMM 0 in R4, so broad prevalence is likely low. For implementers managing medicinal-product or biologically derived substance data, loss of source-material provenance can affect regulatory traceability.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate draft substance source-material content into the R6 `SubstanceDefinition` model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `SubstanceSourceMaterial` in base R6 as a deprecated transitional resource while adding `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal, consolidating immature R4 substance source-material content into the R6 `SubstanceDefinition` model, is reasonable. R4 `SubstanceSourceMaterial` was trial-use/FMM 0, and the R6 package retains a source-material concept only inside `SubstanceDefinition`, so the compatibility obligation is lower than for a mature resource. The breakage is still substantial, but the less-breaking base option would materially undermine the cleanup by preserving a second resource identity for the same domain.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have retained `SubstanceSourceMaterial` as a deprecated R6 resource for one or more releases while introducing `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`. That would let existing R4 instances, generated classes, validators, and endpoints continue to work. This is only a partial alternative because it creates two core ways to represent source-material facts, risks permanent accumulation of deprecated resource shapes, and requires validators, search, examples, and implementer guidance to support both models. Conversion tooling or an external cross-version map would help migration, but those are mitigations rather than a backward-compatible base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves most R4 instances but leaves parallel source-material representations and continued maintenance of a draft/FMM 0 model.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `SubstanceSourceMaterial` with kind `resource`, type `SubstanceSourceMaterial`, baseDefinition `DomainResource`, and abstract `false`.
The assigned R6 StructureDefinition file is absent.
The R6 index contains `StructureDefinition-Substance.json` and `StructureDefinition-SubstanceDefinition.json`, but no `SubstanceSourceMaterial` entry.
R6 defines `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` as an optional `BackboneElement` for material or taxonomic/anatomical source.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment illustrates the breaking mechanism: even minimal R4 content using `resourceType: "SubstanceSourceMaterial"` has no same-resource R6 validation target. A complete production instance may include narrative or other optional metadata, but that does not change the artifact identity break.

findings.narrativeMd: `SubstanceSourceMaterial` is not present as an R6 resource. This is more severe than a field rename: the resource identity itself disappears. Any R4 implementation that exposes this resource as an endpoint, generated model class, persistence table, search target, or validation profile must select a new R6 representation rather than updating element names in place.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `SubstanceSourceMaterial` instance becomes R6-invalid because the R6 core package has no matching StructureDefinition/resource type. Strict parsers may reject the resourceType before element-level validation. Code generators for R6 will not emit the old resource class unless they carry custom legacy definitions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all uses of `SubstanceSourceMaterial` first: persisted resources, API routes, search parameters, generated classes, validation profiles, examples, and transformations. For data migration, evaluate whether each instance belongs inside a `SubstanceDefinition` as `sourceMaterial` plus other R6 elements/extensions. Keep the original R4 resource or an audit copy when traceability is regulatory or safety-relevant, because the candidate R6 component is not a lossless replacement.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal was probably motivated by consolidation of immature medication-definition substance resources into `SubstanceDefinition`. A backward-compatible path was available in principle: keep the resource as deprecated and define transforms. That alternative would have reduced breakage but required the R6 specification to maintain an older draft shape.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official R6 ballot narrative or change logs whether `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` is the intended successor and whether any official conversion map exists outside the local package.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is a real hard break at resource identity level: an R4 instance with `resourceType: "SubstanceSourceMaterial"` has no same R6 StructureDefinition, and generated R6 APIs/endpoints will not expose the old resource class unless they carry a custom legacy definition. I would not elevate the removal to `Revisit` on this finding alone because the R4 artifact was draft/trial-use FMM 0, the domain is specialized, quick public checks did not show clear mainstream production profiling, and R6 keeps a source-material concept inside `SubstanceDefinition`. The migration burden is real, but consolidating a low-maturity standalone resource into a broader substance-definition model appears proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-SubstanceSourceMaterial.json defines a concrete resource with id/type `SubstanceSourceMaterial`, kind `resource`, abstract false, standards-status trial-use, and FMM 0.

The R6 assigned StructureDefinition file is absent; the R6 package index/glob check found `StructureDefinition-Substance.json` and `StructureDefinition-SubstanceDefinition.json` but no `SubstanceSourceMaterial` resource.
R6 `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` exists as optional 0..1 BackboneElement for material or taxonomic/anatomical source.

Targeted web searches for public IG/project production use found no clear mainstream SubstanceSourceMaterial profiles or production deployment evidence; HL7 Europe Base was checked as a broad foundation rather than a specific production profile.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 and trial-use status substantially soften the stability concern. I treated the resource removal as breaking, but not automatically disproportionate without stronger evidence of deployed production use.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: the old resourceType has no R6 validation target, and parsers, validators, servers, searches, serializers, and generated model classes must migrate or carry legacy support.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have retained `SubstanceSourceMaterial` as a deprecated R6 resource while introducing `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`. That would preserve old instances and generated APIs, but it would also preserve a second low-maturity resource identity for the same domain and increase validator, search, documentation, and conversion burden. The alternative exists, but its tradeoffs make the R6 removal/consolidation defensible.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact and partial-alternative judgment: the compatibility mechanism is real, but the prior report gives more weight to broad runtime impact than I would for FMM 0 content with no quick evidence of mainstream production use.

findings.title: R4 source-material detail model is only partially represented by R6 SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial

oldState.summary: R4 has a standalone resource with many source-material, organism, fraction, and part-description fields.

semanticText.definition: R4 captures source material class/type/state, organism identifiers and names, parent substance identifiers/names, origin locations, development stage, fraction descriptions, detailed taxonomy, hybrid data, general organism classification, and anatomical part descriptions.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 model supports repeated `fractionDescription`, repeated `partDescription`, repeated organism authors, parent substance identifiers/names, and several detailed organism taxonomy/hybrid fields.

newState.summary: R6 exposes an optional `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` component with a smaller field set: type, genus, species, part, and countryOfOrigin.

semanticText.definition: Material or taxonomic/anatomical source for the substance.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 candidate is nested in `SubstanceDefinition` and is much narrower than the R4 resource. Several R4 data categories have no direct child in the R6 component.

facts.note: These mappings are inferred by name and definition, not by an official ConceptMap.

facts.oldValue: R4 has repeated `fractionDescription`, repeated `partDescription`, and repeated `organism.author` components.
facts.newValue: R6 `sourceMaterial` is 0..1 and has single `type`, `genus`, `species`, and `part` fields; it has no fractionDescription, partLocation, author, or hybrid subcomponent.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The names, definitions, and R6 source-material ValueSets make `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` the likely destination for some R4 content, but only a subset of R4 elements line up. Without an official map, unmapped fields may belong in other R6 `SubstanceDefinition` structures, extensions, profiles, or retained legacy records.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a migration and codegen break even apart from the root resource removal. Generated R4 code exposes rich nested classes that do not exist under the inferred R6 target. R4 instances using repeated fractions, detailed organism/hybrid taxonomy, parent substance fields, or part locations cannot be mapped into `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` without loss or non-core extensions. Conversely, an R6 `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` is embedded in another resource and has no standard R4 reference relationship back to a standalone `SubstanceSourceMaterial` resource.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Lossy migration of biological source, hybrid, fraction, or anatomical origin data can affect regulatory substance traceability even if the affected resource is specialized.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify and integrate source-material data into the broader SubstanceDefinition model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Carry forward the detailed R4 source-material fields in base R6, either on a deprecated resource or as optional details under `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The compact R6 `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` shape suggests a reasonable goal of simplifying and integrating source-material data. However, the local evidence does not show an official rationale or destinations for many R4 details such as fractions, organism identifiers, hybrid data, detailed taxonomy, parent substances, and part locations. Without that design record, the reasonableness of losing this much base-model fidelity cannot be judged confidently.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have preserved the old detail model as optional deprecated elements, either by retaining the old resource or by adding the detailed children under `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`. That would cover more R4-valid content and reduce data-loss pressure during migration. It is only partial because it would keep a large immature structure in the core model, may overlap with other `SubstanceDefinition` elements, and could leave implementers with both compact and detailed same-domain representations indefinitely. Standard extensions or conversion maps can mitigate loss, but they do not by themselves make base R6 backward compatible.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Improves lossless migration but carries a broad low-maturity content model into R6 and can duplicate or confuse the simplified source-material representation.

evidence.detail: R4 differential declares local fields including sourceMaterialClass/type/state, organismId/name, parentSubstanceId/name, countryOfOrigin, geographicalLocation, developmentStage, fractionDescription, organism, and partDescription subtrees.
R6 `sourceMaterial` has only `type`, `genus`, `species`, `part`, and `countryOfOrigin` local data children.
R6 `Substance` does not contain source-material elements, supporting `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` as the closer migration candidate.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows only the directly mappable subset. R4 state, family, fraction, hybrid, and part-location details require another R6 location, an extension, or retention in a legacy record.

findings.narrativeMd: The R6 candidate does not preserve the R4 resource's content model. R4 treats source-material data as its own resource with detailed substructures. R6 appears to keep only a concise source-material summary inside `SubstanceDefinition`. This will surprise implementers expecting a direct resource rename or a path-only transform.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with detailed but optional source-material content are not directly valid as R6, first because the resource is removed and second because many fields have no equivalent under the inferred R6 target. If implementers choose `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`, strict R6 validation will reject unmapped R4 element names. R6-to-R4 conversion is also not straightforward because the R6 content is embedded in a different resource and does not carry a standalone `SubstanceSourceMaterial` identity or standard back-reference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define an explicit migration policy per old field. Map `sourceMaterialType`, `organism.genus`, `organism.species`, `partDescription.part`, and `countryOfOrigin` to `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` where appropriate. Decide whether sourceMaterialClass/state, organismId/name, parent substance data, geographical location, development stage, fraction data, organism family/intraspecific/author/hybrid/general taxonomy, and partLocation should map to other `SubstanceDefinition` elements, standard/custom extensions, annotations, or retained legacy resources. Test migration with records containing multiple fractions, multiple parts, hybrid organisms, and non-ISO country codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A one-to-one backward-compatible field preservation strategy was available but would have carried a broad, low-maturity R4 model into R6. The chosen model appears cleaner but sacrifices lossless migration unless a standard extension or official map fills the gap.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact intended destinations for unmapped fields should be checked against official substance-definition guidance or work-group change notes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: At the content-model level, `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` is not a lossless successor for the R4 resource. R4 had optional but highly specific source-material fields for class/state, organism identity and name, parent substances, geography, development stage, fractions, detailed taxonomy, hybrid organisms, and part location. The R6 candidate keeps only type, genus, species, part, and country of origin under the sourceMaterial component. A mapper for plasma, vaccine, herbal, or biologically derived substance records would need expert rules to decide which facts can move to generic `SubstanceDefinition` areas, extensions, notes, or retained legacy records. Even with FMM 0, that lossy/expert-dependent migration in a regulatory provenance domain deserves renewed standards attention, at least to confirm intended destinations or add a narrower lossless base path for high-value details.
keyEvidence: R4 local elements include `sourceMaterialClass`, `sourceMaterialState`, `organismId`, `organismName`, repeated `parentSubstanceId/name`, repeated `geographicalLocation`, `developmentStage`, repeated `fractionDescription`, detailed organism taxonomy/author/hybrid/general subtrees, and repeated `partDescription.partLocation`.
R6 `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` children are only `type`, `genus`, `species`, `part`, and repeated `countryOfOrigin`; it is 0..1 as a component.

A search of R6 `SubstanceDefinition` shows generic destinations such as classification, relationship, name, note, and sourceMaterial, but not specific base children for the R4 fraction, hybrid, author, full taxonomy, state, geography, or part-location details.
No local R4/R6 ConceptMap or StructureMap mentioning `SubstanceSourceMaterial` was found in the package ConceptMap/StructureMap files.
R4 definitions explicitly mention regulatory/source-provenance contexts including vaccines, herbal preparations, plasma-derived substances, and the Plasma Master File.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers the expected compatibility obligation and the web search did not establish broad production use. It does not erase the concern because this specific change can be lossy, expert-dependent, and tied to regulatory provenance semantics described in the R4 definitions.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss and runtime/API/codegen: after choosing the inferred R6 target, many old fields have no direct R6 base child, so migration can drop information or require non-core extensions/generic fields; generated R4 nested classes also have no corresponding R6 API surface.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base R6 design could preserve selected detailed optional children under `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`, or retain a deprecated detailed source-material backbone/resource for one transition. The tradeoff is carrying a broad low-maturity model forward and potentially duplicating generic `SubstanceDefinition` mechanisms such as classification or relationship. Still, a narrower optional detail path or explicit computable base mapping looks plausible enough that the design should be revisited.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact and partial-alternative judgment: I agree the migration can be lossy and a partial base alternative exists, but the fresh rationale is more about missing official mapping and expert-dependent regulatory data loss than generic runtime breakage.

findings.title: Likely mapped countryOfOrigin now has a required country ValueSet binding

oldState.summary: R4 `countryOfOrigin` is 0..* `CodeableConcept` with no local binding declared.

binding.description: No local binding appears on the R4 element.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed implementers to encode country of origin using any CodeableConcept coding system or text, subject to profiles outside the base resource.

newState.summary: R6 candidate `countryOfOrigin` remains 0..* `CodeableConcept` but is bound with required strength to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/country|6.0.0-ballot4`.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 binding points to the FHIR country ValueSet, whose local compose includes `urn:iso:std:iso:3166`.

facts.note: The datatype did not materially change for the inferred mapping.
The multiplicity did not materially change for the inferred mapping.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element names and definitions both describe countries where the source material is harvested or sourced. The path changed because the R6 candidate is nested under `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: If an R4 `countryOfOrigin` is migrated to the R6 candidate path, values encoded only with local country code systems, free text, historical country names, or non-ISO jurisdiction concepts may fail required-binding validation. Cardinality and datatype stay compatible, so the risk is terminology conformance rather than structural shape.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Country of origin can matter for plasma, herbal, and biological material traceability; incorrect normalization could change regulatory interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Standardize country-of-origin coding on the common FHIR country ValueSet.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use an extensible rather than required binding for `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial.countryOfOrigin`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Standardizing a country-of-origin element on the common FHIR country ValueSet is a reasonable interoperability goal, and required binding is defensible for a field whose semantics are specifically country or jurisdiction codes. The breakage is limited to migrated values that used local codes, free text, historical labels, or non-country concepts. A less-breaking binding strength exists, but it would not deliver the same strict conformance guarantee.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would be to make the R6 binding extensible, preserving more R4-valid `CodeableConcept` values while still encouraging ISO country codes. This is a partial alternative because extensible binding would permit divergent local codings when implementations claim no suitable ValueSet code, reducing consistent validation and downstream comparability. A published ConceptMap or normalization table would be valuable migration guidance, but it is not itself a backward-compatible base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Accepts more legacy R4 codings and text, but weakens the R6 guarantee that country of origin is drawn from the common country ValueSet.

evidence.detail: R4 `countryOfOrigin` is 0..* `CodeableConcept` with no binding shown on the element.
R6 candidate `countryOfOrigin` has required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/country|6.0.0-ballot4`.
The R6 country ValueSet compose includes system `urn:iso:std:iso:3166`; no expansion was available in the local file.

examples.examplesMd: The invalidity is shown for the inferred R6 target: local country coding that was acceptable in base R4 should be normalized to the required R6 country ValueSet.

findings.narrativeMd: The likely mapped `countryOfOrigin` element keeps the same multiplicity and CodeableConcept datatype, but its terminology contract is much stricter in R6. Implementers that previously used local country codes or free text need normalization rather than a mechanical path move.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: For R4-to-R6 migration into `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial.countryOfOrigin`, strict R6 terminology validation can reject values that are not in the required country ValueSet. R6-to-R4 representation is not structurally difficult because R4 also allows CodeableConcept, but the R4 instance would not preserve the fact that R6 required that code system unless profile metadata is retained.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create a country-code normalization step before R6 validation. Include tests for ISO alpha-2, alpha-3, local-code-only, text-only, historical country, and multi-country examples. If local codes must be retained, keep them as additional codings only when an in-ValueSet coding is also present, or preserve them in an extension/profile-approved coding strategy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This could have been less disruptive with extensible binding, but required binding is a common and defensible choice for countries. The practical compatibility gap should be addressed with a published mapping table rather than weakening all R6 conformance.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm the exact validator behavior for CodeableConcept required bindings in the target implementation, especially text-only CodeableConcepts and multiple codings.

freshReview.narrativeMd: For the inferred mapped path, the datatype and multiplicity remain compatible, but R6 adds a required country ValueSet binding. R4 instances that used local country code systems, text-only country names, historical labels, or non-country jurisdiction concepts may need normalization before strict R6 validation. That is a real terminology migration task, especially because country of origin can matter for plasma and biological material traceability. Still, the field is specifically country/jurisdiction data, the R6 binding uses the common country ValueSet, and weakening it would reduce computable comparability. This looks proportionate rather than a design issue.
keyEvidence: R4 `SubstanceSourceMaterial.countryOfOrigin` is 0..* CodeableConcept with no local binding in the StructureDefinition.
R6 `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial.countryOfOrigin` is 0..* CodeableConcept with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/country|6.0.0-ballot4`.
The local R6 `ValueSet-country.json` compose includes `urn:iso:std:iso:3166`; no local expansion was present.
R4 countryOfOrigin definition mentions countries where plant material is harvested and countries where plasma is sourced for plasma-derived substances.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the stability expectation and keeps this from becoming `Revisit` based only on stricter validation. The regulatory traceability domain keeps it from being `No problem`, but the standardization goal is strong.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: after migration to the inferred R6 path, CodeableConcept values outside the required country ValueSet can fail strict terminology validation even though cardinality and datatype are unchanged.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: An extensible binding would be less-breaking because it could accept more legacy local or text-coded country values while encouraging ISO countries. The tradeoff is that it would not guarantee comparable country coding for a field whose semantics are explicitly country of origin. A normalization map is a useful migration aid, but not a less-breaking base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium-impact and partial-alternative judgment: the break is real but narrower than the resource removal/remodel, and the extensible-binding alternative has a clear conformance tradeoff.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R4 local `SubstanceSourceMaterial` elements do not declare `Reference` types, and the R6 candidate `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` component also has no reference-typed local children.

No local invariants were found on the R4 differential source-material elements or on the R6 candidate sourceMaterial children. Inherited `ele-1`, `ext-1`, and domain-resource constraints are base-artifact scope and excluded.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value was identified on R4 local elements or on the R6 candidate sourceMaterial children.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit was identified for the compared source-material fields.
No local source-material data field changed to a modifier. The only modifier elements observed are inherited `modifierExtension` elements, which are out of scope for this artifact report.

R4 local data elements were marked summary, and the R6 candidate sourceMaterial data children are also summary. Because the artifact was removed as a standalone resource, summary semantics still require migration review, but no mapped child showed a simple summary-flag reversal.
No local slicing was identified on the R4 source-material model or the R6 candidate sourceMaterial component.

Directly mapped candidate fields retain broadly compatible primitive/datatype categories (`CodeableConcept` for type/genus/species/part/country). The main type risk is not datatype replacement but the resource-to-backbone remodel and dropped fields captured in findings.

No directly mapped candidate leaf increases minimum cardinality. However, the remodel collapses repeated R4 structures such as `fractionDescription`, `partDescription`, and `organism.author` into a narrower R6 component; that material risk is captured as a finding.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 candidate source-material fields add example bindings for type, genus, species, and part
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: These bindings use `example` strength, so they do not make otherwise valid instances fail base validation in the same way a required binding would.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: The likely successor area is in active R6 SubstanceDefinition rather than the draft R4 resource
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The status change belongs to the inferred successor resource, not a same-identity `SubstanceSourceMaterial` artifact. The breaking aspect is already captured as removal/remodeling.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The active R6 `SubstanceDefinition` model is likely the durable target for new implementations, but legacy data requires explicit mapping.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` is the strongest local successor candidate and should be assessed in its own resource report for broader substance-definition changes and migration destinations.
Terminology expansions and code-system semantics would improve confidence for migration of source-material type, taxonomy, part, and country values.
A computable cross-version map is needed to decide whether dropped R4 fields should map to other R6 elements, standard extensions, or no R6 representation.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis did not include an official R4-to-R6 diff or change note explaining the removal and intended successor model.
